props.doc: What was broken, in real use.

props.name: change
props.doc: What the change did.

props.name: maintainer
props.doc: The maintainer's own words.

name: ProjectContext
summary: The situation before the work: what existed, what was frustrating or worth testing, and why it was yours to take on. One strong sentence on the left, the rest as prose on the right.
use: Right after ProjectHeader on most work pages (the "IDEA / FRICTION → WOULD THIS WORK?" part of the story).
avoid: Background history nobody needs; restating the header's line.
example: …

props.name: label
props.doc: Small label, default "Context".

props.name: lead
props.doc: The one sentence that frames the problem.

name: ProjectHeader
summary: The top of a work page, in the Work reel's scale: the work's outlined number from the reel (filled pale — this is the work you opened; an event page shows its year instead), type · year, kind, status, the title large, one line, the key facts, roles — and a `media` slot the composition fills however this work needs (art, a screen, nothing).
use: First block of every work page. The title is also the SectionMarker label for the page. Choose `layout` by what leads: `stack` (media below, art-led), `split` (media beside, interface-led), `text` (no media, process-led).
avoid: Stuffing every fact into meta (3–5); a second big title below it.
example:
<ProjectHeader work="z80" layout="split" roles={['Direction', 'Integration']}>
  <MediaFrame slot="media" src="z80/workspace.webp" alt={{ en: 'Z80 Workspace' }} frame="screen" eager />
</ProjectHeader>

props.name: roles
props.doc: The owner's roles, shown as tags.

props.name: quote
props.doc: Show the work's own quote (tagline) under the line. Default true.

name: RefBoard
summary: The opening of a contribution story: the references themselves, very large (#102, #28, #878), each with its repo, its real state and one plain line. Merged ones stand in ink; the rest stay grey, so "merged" and "reported" never read the same.
use: Right after ProjectHeader on a page about work in other people's repos (OSS). Each item jumps to its part of the page (`to`, an #id on the same page); the GitHub links live there, in the PR cards and evidence links.
avoid: Star counts, a heatmap or a trophy wall; calling a report a fix; more than four items (the rest belong lower on the page).
behavior: Aimed at, the number takes the signal color and the line under the item runs out (GoLink). Reduced motion: the same states, no movement.
example:
<RefBoard items={[
  { ref: '#102', repo: 'AgentsMesh', state: { en: 'merged · 21 Jul 2026' }, merged: true, text: { en: 'A read-only check for stale generated files.' }, to: '#agentsmesh' },
  { ref: '#878', repo: 'context-mode', state: { en: 'open · root cause found' }, text: { en: 'Oversized paragraphs slipped past the chunk cap.' }, to: '#context-mode' }
]} />

props.name: items
props.type: { ref: string; repo: string; state: L; merged?: boolean; text: L; to: string }[]

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name of the list.

name: WorkNav
summary: The strip above a work page: "← All work" (goes back to exactly where you were, then locks onto that work), the position among pages `[02] – [03]`, and ↑ ↓ to the neighbouring works with the push transition.
use: Top of every work page — the WorkPage layout renders it.
avoid: Breadcrumb trails; more than one back link.
behavior: Holds still while ↑ ↓ change the work (only the content moves); the first number rolls to the new one.
example: <WorkNav work="z80" order={['vaja', 'z80', 'oss']} />

props.name: order
props.doc: Work ids that have pages, in reading order.

props.name: back
props.doc: Where "All work" goes. Default: the Work page.

props.name: backLabel
props.doc: Its label, when it goes somewhere else (an event page goes back to the Timeline).

name: Atmosphere
summary: The misty ground behind every page: soft gradient + two tiled cloud layers + a tint whose color follows the kind of work in view.
use: Once per page. PageShell already includes it — you normally never place it yourself.
avoid: Adding grain, blobs or extra glow layers (default-deny list). Never put content inside it.
behavior: The tint is identity wash by default. It changes where a composition opts in with `data-fog`, on a page whose PageShell has `fog`, or when a list dispatches `atmo:cat` on document (detail: a category, or null for the page's own — SelectedWork does this for the project in the middle of the screen). A 700ms crossfade changes the tint. On mouse devices, the whole atmosphere drifts at 0.025 × scroll distance as one opaque canvas (after a page change it glides to the new position instead of jumping), and the canvas always reaches the bottom of the screen — even mid-fade, or back on a long page; touch and reduced motion keep it still. Static CSS layers remain visible until the canvas is ready.
example: <section data-cat="game" data-fog>…</section>   (opt-in: only where the work's color should reach the background)

name: Footer
summary: Contact email with copy button, last-updated month, languages.
use: Once per page (PageShell renders it).
avoid: Social icon rows, newsletter forms.
example: <Footer />

name: LanguageToggle

name: LoadLine
summary: Floema's loading line: when a page takes a moment to arrive, a thin line runs across the top while the current page stays on screen — never a blank screen or a spinner.

avoid: Loaders, spinners, percentage counters.

name: PageScrollbar
summary: A page scrollbar at the right edge below the header: grey dashed track, context-colored progress, and a deep cyan cursor in light mode or spark cursor in dark mode.
use: Once per page — PageShell renders it. Drag or click the track to scroll; wheel, touch and keyboard page scrolling still work.
avoid: Placing it beside a visible native scrollbar or inside a section's own scroll area.
behavior: The line thickens on hover and focus. The native scrollbar is hidden only after drag is ready, and remains the fallback when custom styling is unavailable or forced colors are active.

name: Section
summary: A top-level page section: spacing, anchor, SectionHeader, SectionMarker registration. Context color and fog tint are opt-in.

</Section>

props.doc: Vertical SectionMarker label; defaults to `title`. One or two words.

name: SectionHeader
summary: The small title row of a section: optional index, mono title, optional count, optional one-line description. Carries no layout of its own.
use: At the top of any section. <Section> renders one for you; use it directly when a composition needs the header somewhere unusual (inside a pinned strip, beside media).
avoid: Big display headings for sections (one statement per page); descriptions longer than one sentence.
example: <SectionHeader index="02" title={{ en: 'Sheets, frames, captures' }} />

props.doc: Section number, e.g. "02".

props.doc: Shows `[04]` at the right end.

props.doc: One sentence under the title.

props.name: as
props.doc: Heading level. Default h2.

props.name: trigger
props.doc: Register as the SectionMarker trigger of the enclosing [data-mark] element. Default true.

name: SectionMarker
summary: A vertical label that sticks to the top-left corner once a section's own horizontal title has scrolled under the header, with a progress line for that section.
use: Once per page (PageShell renders it). Any element with `data-mark="Label"` becomes a stop; its title is the child with `data-mark-trigger` (else its first h1/h2). <Section> and <ProjectHeader> set these for you.
avoid: Marking small blocks — only sections at least ~1 screen tall. Hidden below 760px (the gutter is too narrow).
behavior: Appears with a top-down wipe (500ms enter), disappears in 60ms, swaps label with exit → wipe. Progress fill uses the section's context color (identity blue, or the work's kind inside a work).

name: SiteNav
summary: Thin sticky header: name mark (the first name, which turns into the owner's handwriting when pointed at), main nav with a sliding cursor, language switch, theme toggle.
use: Once per page (PageShell renders it). PageShell passes `nav` through as `current`.
avoid: Adding more than ~5 nav items, or icons — on phones the menu is a text button (MENU), never an icon-only hamburger.
behavior: The name mark, pointed at or focused, is written over by the owner's handwriting in the identity blue: one soft edge travels left → right, the typed name giving way behind it (Thai pages: the Thai signature; reduced motion: an instant swap; touch: stays typed). Cursor slides to the hovered item (240ms) and back; a clicked item becomes current at once. Desktop links have a wider click target from 960px. Phones (≤760px): one thin row — name + a MENU button; the button drops a panel under the header (the nav as 48px rows, language and theme below it; items come in one after another), closed by the button, Esc, a tap outside or choosing a page; the page does not scroll while it is open and focus stays inside. On pages that contain the nav's #anchors, it follows the section in view (scroll-spy). Stays still during page transitions.
example: <SiteNav current="work" />

props.name: current
props.doc: Key of the active nav item: 'work' | 'about' | 'timeline' (see NAV in src/lib/site.ts). Home has none: the name mark is its link.

name: ThemeToggle
summary: Cycles Auto → Light → Dark. Auto follows the device. Remembered per browser.
use: Inside SiteNav (already there).
avoid: Sun/moon icons without text.
behavior: Switching: a plane in the new mode's ground slides in from the right (the toggle's side) on the click, covers the page, the theme switches underneath, and the plane slides on out to the left (~0.8s, soft 10° edges, transform only — no page capture; scripts/theme.ts). Nothing inside the page animates while it switches. A step that does not change what shows (Auto → Light on a light device) just changes the setting. Reduced motion: instant.
example: <ThemeToggle />
